name: Cardiotocography (Intrapartum Electronic Fetal Monitoring and FIGO Classification)

reference.source: Sakshi Arora Obstetrics 9th Edition / FIGO Consensus Guidelines on Intrapartum Monitoring
clinicalPearls: Normal baseline fetal heart rate is 110 to 160 beats per minute with normal baseline variability of 5 to 25 bpm
Early decelerations mirror uterine contractions caused by benign physiological fetal head compression
Late decelerations start after contraction peak, reflecting uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal hypoxia
Variable decelerations feature abrupt drop caused by umbilical cord compression, relieved by maternal repositioning
Sinusoidal pattern is a regular smooth sine-wave oscillation pathognomonic for severe fetal anemia
reference.pathophysiology: Cardiotocography continuously monitors fetal heart rate and uterine contractions to detect intrapartum hypoxia. Baseline heart rate reflects intrinsic SA node pacemaking modulated by sympathetic and parasympathetic autonomic balance. Variability reflects healthy autonomic tone and intact brainstem oxygenation. Uterine contractions temporarily compress intramyometrial spiral arterioles; in uteroplacental insufficiency, transient chemoreceptor-mediated vagal deceleration produces late decelerations.
additionalDifferentials: Normal physiological CTG versus suspicious versus pathological trace
Early deceleration (head compression) versus late deceleration (hypoxia)
Sinusoidal pattern (severe anemia) versus pseudosinusoidal (maternal narcotics)
Fetal sleep state versus pathological absent variability
additionalInvestigations: Fetal scalp blood sampling for pH (abnormal < 7.20) or lactate (> 4.8 mmol/L)
Ultrasound Doppler assessment of fetal vessels in high-risk labor
